tool_input.description: Investigate Calendar.setTimeZone behavior on cloned calendar

result:
No scratch files left, and `_tools/out` is just the compiled test output from the run. Everything is clean.

Created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/FastDatePrinterAgentTest.java` with 37 self-contained JUnit 5 tests covering `FastDatePrinter`: basic/empty patterns, illegal pattern chars, ISO-8601 (`X`/`XX`/`XXX`) and `Z`/`ZZ`/`ZZZ` zone rules, 12/24-hour midnight boundaries, day-of-week wraparound, week-year computation, two/four-digit year wrapping and padding (including 5-digit years and values ≥100 not being truncated), month/weekday text variants, quoted literals with escaped quotes, calendar/timezone interaction semantics, all `format` overloads, `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString`, null-argument behavior, serialization round-trip, `parseToken`, `getTimeZoneDisplay`, and the internal cache `clear()`. No lambdas, diamond operators, or try-with-resources were used, per the Java 8 constraint. All 37 tests pass via `./_tools/test.sh`.
